## Progress

- Merged [PR #27](https://github.com/ALFRED-LUCIFER/medvya/pull/27): Tenant/Facility/Membership, EF global filters + SQL Server row-level security on SESSION_CONTEXT (FILTER + BLOCK predicates)
- Testcontainers tests on SQL Server 2022: cross-tenant reads blocked with filters off and with raw SQL, cross-tenant writes/moves blocked, no tenant = no rows, 100 pooled connections without leaks; mutation-checked (RLS off → 4/5 fail). Satisfies P0 exit criterion 3
- Also pinned System.Security.Cryptography.Pkcs 10.0.13 (CVE-2026-70162)

## Description

Organisation (tenant) → facility → membership model. `tenant_id` (PRD: clinic_id) on every clinic-owned table. A DbConnection interceptor sets SESSION_CONTEXT(N'tenant_id') read-only on every open from the authenticated membership; a SQL security policy applies FILTER and BLOCK predicates; EF Core global query filters mirror it. One user can hold memberships in several clinics; the active facility is chosen at sign-in.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] **AC1.** Given two tenants with data, when user A of tenant 1 queries any tenant-owned table, then no row of tenant 2 is returned, even when the EF query filter is disabled with IgnoreQueryFilters() (RLS still blocks).
- [ ] **AC2.** Inserting or updating a row with another tenant's tenant_id is blocked by the BLOCK predicate.
- [ ] **AC3.** A user with memberships in two clinics sees only the active facility's tenant data and can switch facility, which re-establishes session context.
- [ ] **AC4.** Session context is reset on every pooled connection open (test opens 100 pooled connections alternating tenants with zero leaks).
- [ ] **AC5.** The cross-tenant read/write test runs in CI on every PR and fails the build on any leak (P0 exit gate 3).

## Definition of Done

All acceptance criteria above, **plus** the cross-cutting X1–X8 checklist in [docs/05-delivery](../../docs/05-delivery/README.md#definition-of-done-every-ticket).
